newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL DROPS ON GAS PRICE, MKT ASSESSES EFFECT.
newsitem.headline: MOL DROPS ON GAS PRICE, MKT ASSESSES EFFECT.

text.p: Shares of Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt dropped on Monday some 90 forints following the announcement of an 11.3 percent gas price increase, analysts said.
"The market knew that MOL had requested an 18 percent increase and...it is very likely that the (share) price dropped due to the announcement," said Ferenc Szolosi of Postabank Securities.
On Monday the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism announced its quarterly energy price increase of 11.3 percent for gas prices and 4.5 percent for electricity prices.
Szolosi said the market was still assessing the effect of the new gas price on MOL, but added he saw support for the paper at around 4,000 forints.
"I do not think that it (MOL) would stay below 4,000 forints for a long time," he said.
He also said that although the gas price increase was not as high as expected, it was significantly higher than the quarterly forint devaluation of 3.3 percent.
"I don't know whether this increase will make MOL's gas business profiatble, but it certainly is a serious step forward," Szolosi said.
At 1013 GMT, MOL shares stood at 4,010 forints on the Budapest Stock Exchange, down 80.
